# Claude Code Permissions and Sandbox

Permissions decide which tool calls Claude Code may run, which need a prompt, and which it must refuse.
The sandbox adds a second wall around `Bash` commands, at the level of the operating system.
For example, an `allow` rule for `Bash(npm test)` runs the tests with no prompt, and the sandbox still limits what that command can reach.

## Marks

| Mark | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| ✅ | A page of the [Claude Code docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) names it. |
| 🔍 | Only the Claude Code bundle names it. No docs page does. |
| ⚠️ | The docs and the bundle differ. The row says how. |
| 🧪 | It works only behind a flag, a plan, or a server-side switch. The row says which. |
| ❌ | It is removed or does nothing in `2.1.303`. |
